question: A department sets the deepest-reasoning model as the default for all of its work, including short routine replies. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Short replies will be written at greater length than the person asking the question wanted.
B) Routine work consumes far more allowance, so it runs out during the work that actually needs it.
C) Short replies will come back noticeably slower, which colleagues will find frustrating to work with.
D) The department will be unable to switch to a lighter model once a default has been set for it.
correct_answers: B) Routine work consumes far more allowance, so it runs out during the work that actually needs it.
explanations: Incorrect. Response length is controlled by the request, not by the tier, and it is easy to correct.
Correct. The deepest tier uses meaningfully more of the usage allowance per message, so spending it on trivial work leaves less available for the genuinely hard problems.
Incorrect. Slower replies are an annoyance rather than the substantive cost of this policy.
Incorrect. The model can be changed at any time, so nothing about the choice is locked in.
